title: He Signed Every Letter… The Zodiac Was Never Caught
lines: He mailed a newspaper a torn piece of his victim's shirt. Then he signed the letter. This is the Zodiac speaking. Over fifty years later, nobody knows who he was.
Northern California, December 1968. A teenage couple on their first date parked on a quiet road outside Benicia. They were both shot. There were no witnesses.
Seven months later, the Fourth of July, 1969. Another couple, another parked car, in Vallejo. The young woman died. The man survived.
Less than an hour later, a man called the Vallejo police. Calmly, he said he did it. And the first couple too. Then he hung up.
And then he did something no killer had ever done before.
He mailed three newspapers one third each of a secret code. Four hundred and eight symbols. Print it on your front page, he warned, or I kill again.
In his next letter, he gave himself a name. This is the Zodiac speaking.
Days later, a schoolteacher and his wife in Salinas cracked the code. It said he liked killing people. But he would not give his real name.
September 1969, Lake Berryessa. He came in daylight, in a black hood with a white crosshair on the chest. Another young couple. Only the man survived.
Before he left, he walked to their car and wrote on the door. The dates of every attack. And his symbol.
Two weeks later, San Francisco. A cab driver was shot in a wealthy neighborhood. But this time, there were witnesses.
Police raced to the scene. Two officers passed a man walking calmly away. But the radio had given the wrong description. So they let him go.
Days later, the Chronicle opened an envelope. Inside was a piece of the driver's shirt. And a threat to attack a school bus.
Then came a second code. Three hundred and forty symbols. For fifty one years, nobody could crack it.
In December 2020, three amateur codebreakers finally did. He hoped we were having fun trying to catch him. And he was not afraid of the gas chamber.
He claimed thirty seven victims. Police can confirm five dead and two survivors. Then, by 1974, the letters just stopped.
Police had one main suspect, Arthur Leigh Allen. But his prints, his handwriting, and a partial DNA test didn't match. He died in 1992, never charged.

The case is still open. Who do you think the Zodiac was? Tell me in the comments. Then watch our short on the killer who drank with the cops hunting him. And follow for a new unsolved mystery every day.

notes: Sources: Wikipedia 'Zodiac Killer'; FBI San Francisco statement on the 340 cipher (Dec 2020); SFPD/Vallejo PD records via Wikipedia. Lake Herman Rd, Benicia, 20 Dec 1968 (first date, both teens shot). Blue Rock Springs, Vallejo, 4-5 Jul 1969 (woman died, man survived); call to Vallejo PD ~12:40 AM claiming both attacks. 31 Jul 1969 letters to Vallejo Times-Herald, SF Chronicle, SF Examiner each with 1/3 of the 408 cipher; front-page demand. Letter received 7 Aug 1969 opened 'This is the Zodiac speaking' (first use of the name). 8 Aug 1969 Donald & Bettye Harden of Salinas solved the 408 ('I like killing people...', 'I will not give you my name'). Lake Berryessa 27 Sep 1969 ~6:30 PM, hooded costume with crossed-circle symbol; woman died, man survived; wrote dates and symbol on the car door. 11 Oct 1969 cab driver shot in Presidio Heights, teen witnesses; officers Fouke/Zelms passed a man after a dispatch with the wrong description. 13 Oct letter to the Chronicle with a swatch of the driver's shirt and a school-bus threat; opened 'This is the Zodiac speaking'. 340 cipher mailed Nov 1969, solved Dec 2020 by Oranchak, Blake, Van Eycke ('I hope you are having lots of fun in trying to catch me', 'not afraid of the gas chamber'). 1974 letter claimed 37; 5 confirmed killed, 2 survived. Arthur Leigh Allen: prints, handwriting, 2002 partial DNA did not match; died 1992, never charged. Case open (SFPD, FBI). Victim names and photos left out on purpose (respectful, advertiser-friendly).
